clue.text: Prosperous couple eschewing whiskey visiting fine party

indicators.note: to eschew is to avoid or go without, so the following letter is dropped
a visitor goes inside someone's place, so this piece sits within the others

blocks.note: fine, as in feeling fine or well
a couple is two
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A wealthy pair turn down the whisky as they drop in on a smart party.
explanation.walkthrough: Whiskey is the NATO alphabet's W; 'visiting' puts the shortened couple inside the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-to-do is comfortably off, with plenty of money: a standard idiom for wealthy.

clue.text: Daughter in African country downing port, getting tense

indicators.note: downing something knocks it out, so the next word's letters are removed
in places the first piece inside the remaining letters

blocks.note: Egypt is a country in north-east Africa
PT is a standard abbreviation for port
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A daughter in Africa knocks back some port and starts feeling anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like a drink being downed, but it is just the two-letter abbreviation struck out of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy describes someone nervous and on edge, a common synonym for anxious or uneasy.

clue.text: Urges uprooting six herbs

indicators.note: uprooting pulls something out entirely, so these letters are taken away

blocks.note: to chivvy is to nag or urge someone on
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A gardening instruction: pull up six plants of a herb.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking VI out of CHIVVIES leaves CHIVES; 'uprooting' fits the garden picture neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Chives are slender onion-flavoured plants grown and used in cooking as a culinary herb.

clue.text: Draw on some revolting cigarettes I lit up

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used
revolting means turning over, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the last three words

explanation.surface: Someone takes a drag on a few nasty cigarettes they have just lit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like disgust at the cigarettes but signals reading backwards; 'Draw on' suggests smoking but means make use of.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw on resources is to make use of them, which is exactly what utilise means.

clue.text: Twice prevent Scotsmen establishing rugby club

blocks.note: to bar is to prevent, written twice
Ian is a typically Scottish first name, so Scotsmen are Ians

explanation.surface: Two refusals stop some Scots from setting up a rugby team.
explanation.walkthrough: The Barbarians are a famous British invitational rugby union team made up of guest players.
explanation.definitionFit: The Barbarians are a well-known invitation-only rugby union side, so the proper name fits the club.

clue.text: Pasty-faced old man in retirement departs unwell

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the following letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
unwell simply means ill

explanation.surface: A retired old man leaves looking sickly and pale.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the last two pieces are turned round; the old man stays at the front as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallid means pale and lacking healthy colour, the same as having a pasty complexion.

clue.text: School principal's attractive-looking passport photo?

blocks.note: the head of a school, with the possessive
hot is slang for attractive

explanation.surface: Admiring the good-looking photo in the headteacher's passport.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a passport photo is just one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A headshot is a photograph of someone's face and shoulders, the kind required for official ID documents.

clue.text: Plays with Rose maybe, almost securing par to finish

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final part is cut off
to finish points to the closing letter of the word before
securing means holding something firmly inside

blocks.note: the damask is a type of rose
the last letter of par

explanation.surface: A golf scene: playing with Justin Rose, almost making par on the final hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like the golfer, given 'par', but is the flower; DAMASK loses its last two letters and takes R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Dramas are plays or theatrical works, so the plural nouns are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Rejecting arson at first, regarded wrecked ship

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of the preceding word
rejecting means throwing out, so this letter is removed
something wrecked is broken up and left in disorder

blocks.note: the opening letter of arson
taken as written

explanation.surface: Arson having been ruled out, the shipwreck is regarded as an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A out of REGARDED and rearrange the remaining seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dredger is a vessel that scoops mud and silt from the bottom of harbours and rivers.

clue.text: Cassius perhaps put forward to succeed Caesar originally

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the name before it
to succeed is to follow after, so this piece comes second

blocks.note: the first letter of Caesar
to lay a proposal is to put it forward

explanation.surface: Cassius proposed as Caesar's successor, as in Roman intrigue.
explanation.walkthrough: Cassius conspired against Julius Caesar, so the surface reads as Roman politics, but the definition is the boxer Cassius Clay.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassius Clay was the birth name of boxer Muhammad Ali, so this is an example of a surname.

clue.text: Order lovely book backed by everyone in sport

indicators.note: to order is to arrange, so these letters are put into a new sequence
backed by means supported from behind, so the next piece follows on after

blocks.note: taken as written
B is an abbreviation for book
everyone means all

explanation.surface: Ordering a lovely book on sport that everyone backs.
explanation.definitionFit: Volleyball is a team game in which a ball is hit over a high net by hand.

clue.text: Garden flower, repeatedly reduced, was the dearest one

indicators.note: reduced twice over: each of two words is cut short by its last letter

blocks.note: the priciest item cost most

explanation.surface: A garden flower, marked down again and again, had been the priciest plant on sale.
explanation.walkthrough: COST and MOST each lose their final T.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmos is a popular annual bedding plant with daisy-like blooms grown in gardens.

clue.text: Regular rite with common changes

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters are altered into a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A routine ceremony, altered in the usual way.
explanation.definitionFit: Metronomic means steady and evenly paced, like a metronome's beat, hence regular.

clue.text: Ennobled business magnate, outwardly embarrassed given sweetener?

indicators.note: outwardly keeps just the outside letters of the word that follows

blocks.note: Alan Sugar, the British businessman and TV star, was made Lord Sugar
the first and last letters of embarrassed

explanation.surface: A tycoon peer, red-faced on being handed a little bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Sugar is a businessman known from the UK version of The Apprentice; 'sweetener' also hints at a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sugared has had sweet stuff added to it, a playful reading of having received a sweetener.

clue.text: Film season Labour leader introduces

indicators.note: introducing something means going in front of it, so this piece comes first

blocks.note: Michael Foot led the UK Labour Party from 1980 to 1983
to season timber or cheese is to let it age

explanation.surface: A film about the season a Labour leader launches.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Foot was leader of Britain's Labour Party in the early 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Footage is recorded film or video material, so as a noun it means film.

clue.text: Sting, say, regularly behind crooner given grand for turning up

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter at even intervals
given means one more piece is added on
in a down clue turning up means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: The singer Sting, often turning up just behind a crooner on the bill with a grand fee.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting the musician comes from Newcastle; a Geordie is a native of Tyneside, so 'Sting, say' is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Sting was born in Wallsend near Newcastle, making him a native of Tyneside by birth.

clue.text: Extent of bloomer possibly starts to terrify her

indicators.note: starts picks the opening letter of each word that follows

blocks.note: a bloomer is a crusty loaf, so an example of bread
the first letters of terrify and her

explanation.surface: How big a blunder might scare her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake but is a British loaf with a rounded top.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadth is the width or scope of something, so it is a synonym for range or extent.

clue.text: Indian cooking method using both ends of tomato Ms Day peeled

indicators.note: peeling removes the skin, so the outside letters go

blocks.note: the two ends of tomato are T and O, written out with the word between them
Doris Day, the American singer and actress

explanation.surface: Doris Day cooking an Indian dish from tomatoes she has peeled.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'both ends' is spelt out literally: T, AND, O.
explanation.definitionFit: Tandoori is food cooked in a tandoor, a clay oven used in Indian and Pakistani cuisine.

clue.text: Sort of car criminals use? Well, I never!

blocks.note: first meaning: the vehicle robbers flee in
second meaning: an exclamation of disbelief, said as two words

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation is written as two words, but the enumeration runs them together as one.
explanation.definitionFit: A getaway car is used for escaping a crime, and 'get away!' expresses surprised disbelief.

clue.text: Advertise upgrade

blocks.note: first meaning: publicise a product
second meaning: raise someone to a higher rank

explanation.definitionFit: Marketing a product and moving an employee to a higher job are both expressed by this verb.

clue.text: Satisfy requests, ending in gratitude

indicators.note: ending in picks out the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: pleas are appeals or requests
the last letter of gratitude

explanation.surface: Meeting people's requests, which ends in their thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface tempts a reading of 'please' as the polite word, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to make them happy or content, which is the verb sense of satisfy.

clue.text: Thought Rob must admit guilt

indicators.note: admitting someone lets them in, so the next piece goes inside

blocks.note: to mug is to rob someone in the street
sin is wrongdoing, and so guilt

explanation.surface: A thought: Rob has to confess he did it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rob' poses as a man's name but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Musing is reflective contemplation, so the noun means a thought or meditation.

clue.text: Latest way to overcome hernia essentially

indicators.note: in a down clue, overcoming means sitting on top of, so this piece goes first
essentially means at its core, so only the central letters are used

blocks.note: a mode is a way or method
the middle two letters of hernia

explanation.surface: The newest technique for beating a hernia.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means current or up to date, so it shares the sense of most recent.

clue.text: Indirectly support round of applause

blocks.note: to second a motion is to support it
give them a hand means applaud

explanation.surface: Backing a round of applause in a roundabout way.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing news secondhand means getting it via another person rather than directly from the source.

clue.text: Nameless benefactor's exit point?

indicators.note: nameless means without a name, so the abbreviation for name is removed

blocks.note: a benefactor gives money, like a donor
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An anonymous donor quietly slips out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nameless benefactor' reads as an anonymous donor, but it means remove N; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A door is the opening through which people leave a room or building, so it serves as a way out.

clue.text: Bird swooped in New York?

blocks.note: first meaning: a pigeon-like bird, symbol of peace
second meaning: American past tense of dive

explanation.walkthrough: In American English the past tense of dive is commonly this word rather than 'dived'; New York stands for US usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a small pigeon-family bird, while the US past tense of plunge downward matches swooped.

clue.text: Each holding tears back makes wish

indicators.note: holding something keeps it inside, so one piece wraps the other
back tells us the whole assembly is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: EA is the abbreviation for each
tears in cloth are rips

explanation.surface: Each person holding back tears makes a wish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' wants to be crying, but it is the sense of splits in fabric, and 'back' turns the whole assembly round.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to hope or long for something ambitious, a verb close in sense to want.

clue.text: Creature that all other animals go after?

definitions.text: Creature that all other animals go after?

blocks.clueFragment: Creature that all other animals go after?
blocks.note: surface reading: a beast that every other species hunts
setter's reading: in an alphabetical list of animals, this one comes first, so every other follows it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go after' suggests chasing, but it means coming later in the dictionary order.
explanation.definitionFit: This African burrowing mammal heads alphabetical lists of animal names because of its double A start.
